title: Exact residue obstruction for meromorphic Abelian differentials on the Riemann sphere with one zero and only simple poles
author: Quentin Gendron; Guillaume Tahar
difficulty_reason: The residue theorem only gives the sum-zero constraint and does not characterize the exceptional integral resonances for a single zero. The authors construct and recognize weighted connection trees by gluing flat polar domains, then prove commensurability of every excluded configuration and the sharp integer total bound through leaf-removal induction. The reverse saddle-connection-length argument supplies the full obstruction rather than merely a sufficient gluing recipe.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. The single-zero part of Theorem1.2(ii): s≥3 simple poles and one zero of order s−2 on a variable genus-zero compact Riemann surface. Nonzero complex residue tuples sum to0; excluded tuples are precisely nonzero complex multiples of primitive signed positive-integer tuples whose positive sum equals the negative absolute sum and is≤s−2. The author convention is residues multiplied by2pi i; exact source convention retained. Complete new flat connection-tree existence/equivalence, commensurability induction, integer normalization and converse saddle-length obstruction read. Existing flat polar-domain dictionary is explicit, with gluing constructions written out. No all-zero/non-simple-pole, multi-zero stable-degeneration or higher-genus connected-component parameter variant separately counted.
